Thought: The wavenumber of the carbonyl stretching mode is influenced by the nature of the substituents attached to the carbonyl group. Electronegative substituents increase the wavenumber, while less electronegative or bulkier substituents decrease it. The compounds given have substituents with different halogen atoms: fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), and iodine (I). Fluorine is the most electronegative, followed by chlorine, bromine, and iodine. Therefore, the compound with fluorine substituents will have the highest wavenumber, and the one with iodine will have the lowest. The correct order of increasing wavenumber is: iodine < bromine < chlorine < fluorine.
